sub_scenario.family: communicating uncertainty and risk escalation in cross-functional decisions
sub_scenario.one_line: university research partnerships director: predict rejection of the immediate-commitment format

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the collaboration register and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The faculty calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can speak with a faculty lead in the afternoon when the proposed scope has been agreed.
Do afternoon conversations prevent collaboration?
No, settled matters are easy to discuss.
Someone new shadowed me in the partnership office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the grant round into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
At a donor partnership call, I said a department would provide facilities before separating one professor's interest from a signed institutional commitment, and we had to retract the statement.
What did that teach you?
Interest must not be presented as approval.
I can run a useful morning proposal review by labelling confirmed commitments and tentative interests.
Why make that distinction?
It prevents a promising conversation from becoming an unauthorized promise.
I archived last cycle's notes on the faculty calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
By 15:30, after grant correspondence, I am less reliable at holding several qualification details in mind.
Would a scripted agenda solve everything?
Not if the group expects an immediate commitment.
A vendor call about the collaboration register ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the partnership office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the grant round.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the faculty calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The provost asks how you would react to daily 15:30 office hours for ambiguous cross-faculty escalations, where attendees expect a named owner before documents are checked.
How would you react?
I would decline that format because it invites the same kind of premature commitment.
I sketched next week's plan for the grant round before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the collaboration register updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The research office can schedule a 10:00 review with a commitment log and a next-day confirmation step.
Would that be different?
Yes, it would let us distinguish interest from authorization.
A dean says accepting the office hour would demonstrate that partnerships move quickly.
Does that change your likely response?
No, moving quickly cannot justify representing an unconfirmed commitment as settled.
I closed the week by updating the partnership office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
How would I likely react to the proposed 15:30 cross-faculty escalation office hour that expects immediate ownership before documents are checked?
